prompt: Build, from scratch, a single self-contained HTML page called audio-visualizer.html that shows a music visualiser driven entirely by synthetic maths - there is no microphone, no audio file and no Web Audio graph anywhere on the page. On a dark stage a row of spectrum bars rises and falls to a steady beat, each bar carrying a peak cap that jumps up on a hit and then slides down until the next one, a waveform ribbon runs across the stage, and a pulse marks every beat onset. Bass bands are visibly louder than treble, the whole piece is a seamless loop of a whole number of beats, and a small readout shows the tempo and the band count. Write your own implementation; do not copy any existing code.
definition_of_done:
final_output_file: audio-visualizer.html, one self-contained HTML page. All cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. Numbered, each one measured by one test:
1. The page starts with <!doctype html> and contains a <canvas>.
2. It makes ZERO external requests: no http(s) or protocol-relative src or href, no @import, no url(//...), no fetch, no XMLHttpRequest. Everything inline.
3. The signal is synthetic, not captured: the page never mentions getUserMedia, mediaDevices, MediaStream, AudioContext, decodeAudioData, createAnalyser, an <audio> element or new Audio().
4. Animation is driven by requestAnimationFrame.
5. The pure model lives in <script id="spectrum-model" type="module"> and mentions none of getContext, document., window. or canvas - it is run standalone in node by the gate.
6. The renderer, outside that block, calls spectrum(, peaks(, waveform( and beat( so every model output reaches the canvas.
7. BANDS is between 24 and 256; spectrum(t) returns exactly BANDS finite magnitudes, each within 0..1.
8. Bass dominates treble: the mean of the lowest quarter of bands exceeds 1.5x the mean of the highest quarter, and the treble is not silent.
9. BEAT_PERIOD is a musical period between 0.25 and 2.0 seconds; at each of the first 8 beat onsets the summed spectrum exceeds 1.4x its value at the last sample before the next onset, and beat(t) exceeds 0.5 at that onset.
10. LOOP is a whole number of BEAT_PERIODs and spectrum(t) equals spectrum(t + LOOP) band for band.
11. peaks(t) never rises inside a beat and its sum at the end of each beat is below 0.95x its sum at the onset.
12. peaks(t) is never below spectrum(t) for the same band and time.
13. waveform(t, n) returns exactly n finite samples inside -1..1 whose range exceeds 0.2.
If the contract cannot be satisfied, return status='failure' with the precise reason rather than a page that games the tests.
contract:
Return ONE complete HTML document in the `code` field, from <!doctype html> to </html>, saved as audio-visualizer.html. Structure it as model plus renderer:
1. <script id="spectrum-model" type="module"> containing ONLY pure maths. It must export the constants BANDS (integer, 24-256), BEAT_PERIOD (seconds) and LOOP (seconds), and the pure deterministic functions spectrum(t) -> array of BANDS magnitudes in 0..1, peaks(t) -> array of BANDS cap heights in 0..1, beat(t) -> a single 0..1 pulse strength, and waveform(t, n) -> array of n samples in -1..1. The words getContext, document., window. and canvas must not appear anywhere in this block: the gate extracts it, writes it as model.mjs and imports it in node with no DOM.
2. A separate <script> that owns the <canvas id="stage">, sizes it to the viewport, and on each requestAnimationFrame calls spectrum, peaks, waveform and beat for the elapsed time and draws bars, caps, ribbon and beat pulse.
Model requirements: deterministic for a given t, since the gate samples the same times twice; a spectral tilt so low bands carry more energy than high ones; a per-beat envelope that attacks on the onset and decays before the next; caps that hold above their bars and only ever fall between onsets; and exact periodicity over LOOP, which must be a whole number of beats.
Render requirements: dark background, one bar per band with its cap drawn above it, a waveform ribbon, a visible pulse on each beat, and a small HUD reading out the tempo and the band count. Forbidden anywhere on the page: network access of any kind, external fonts, images or scripts, any library or framework, the Web Audio API, microphone or media capture, and any <audio> element.
